hits.name: multiple myeloma
hits.description: A bone marrow-based plasma cell neoplasm characterized by a serum monoclonal protein and skeletal destruction with osteolytic lesions, pathological fractures, bone pain, hypercalcemia, and anemia. Clinical variants include non-secretory myeloma, smoldering myeloma, indolent myeloma, and plasma cell leukemia. (WHO, 2001)

hits.name: asymptomatic myeloma
hits.description: A plasma cell myeloma lacking clinical manifestations and organ impairment.

hits.name: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B
hits.description: Multiple endocrine neoplasia 2B (MEN2B) syndrome is a rare aggressive form of MEN2 characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, mucosal ganglioneuroma, and marfanoid habitus.

hits.name: Ovarian Endometrioid Adenocarcinoma with Squamous Differentiation
hits.description: An endometrioid adenocarcinoma that arises from the ovary and exhibits squamous differentiation. The squamous cell component often has a cytologically benign appearance.

hits.name: Persistent patent ductus venosus
hits.description: Persistence of blood flow through the ductus venosus for longer than the normal time after birth.

hits.name: epithelial skin neoplasm
hits.description: A epithelial neoplasm that involves the zone of skin.

hits.name: skin carcinoma
hits.description: A carcinoma that arises from epithelial cells of the zone of skin

hits.name: non-melanoma skin carcinoma
hits.description: Any skin carcinoma that is not melanoma, with the most common types being basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma

hits.name: keratinocyte carcinoma
hits.description: A skin cancer arising from the keratin-producing cells of the epidermis. The term encompasses both basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma.

hits.name: basal cell neoplasm
hits.description: A neoplastic proliferation of basal cells in the epidermis (part of the skin) or other anatomic sites (most frequently the salivary glands). The basal cell neoplastic proliferation in the epidermis results in basal cell carcinomas. The basal cell neoplastic proliferation in the salivary glands can be benign, resulting in basal cell adenomas or malignant, resulting in basal cell adenocarcinomas.
